title: Does Your Business Need a Better Network for AI? Here’s How to Tell
summary: Every AI depends on a strong network. Discover how to prepare your business network for AI and identify gaps before they slow you down.
body_markdown:
#


If you’re planning to use AI, your network for AI is just as important as the software itself. Every AI application depends on moving data quickly, securely, and reliably between people, devices, cloud services, and business systems. If the network struggles to keep up, AI becomes slower, less reliable, and harder for employees to trust.


Many businesses are already facing that challenge. Cisco’s 2026 AI Readiness Index found that only 34% of organizations have the infrastructure needed to scale AI. The same report found that only 12% are prepared for modern risks such as unpatched vulnerabilities, compliance gaps, and legal exposure. Businesses are adopting AI faster than they are modernizing the infrastructure that supports it.


The good news is that preparing your business network for AI doesn’t always mean replacing everything you already own. It starts with understanding what AI expects from your network and identifying where your infrastructure may need to improve.


## What Is an AI-Ready Network?


An AI-ready network allows AI applications to communicate with users, devices, cloud platforms, and business systems without delays or interruptions.


Think of your network as the highway system that keeps your business moving. Every time an employee asks an AI assistant a question, an AI receptionist answers a customer call, or a reporting tool analyzes business data, information travels across your network. The faster and more reliably that information moves, the better the AI experience becomes.


An AI-ready network is designed to handle these larger workloads while keeping other business applications running smoothly. It provides the bandwidth, reliability, security, and performance that modern AI tools require.


## Why Are So Many Businesses Struggling with AI?


Many business owners assume AI success depends on choosing the right software. While selecting the right tools is important, software can only perform as well as the infrastructure supporting it.


Most business networks were designed years ago to handle email, web browsing, file sharing, and video meetings. AI creates a different kind of workload. Instead of sending relatively small amounts of data throughout the day, AI applications often process large volumes of information in real time while communicating continuously with cloud services and other business systems.


As organizations add AI-powered customer service, meeting assistants,[voice agents](https://sangoma.com/blog/why-voice-is-becoming-important-again-in-the-era-of-ai-agents/) , security cameras, automation platforms, and connected devices, the amount of network traffic grows quickly. If the network cannot keep pace, employees often experience slow responses, unreliable applications, and inconsistent performance.


Those problems point to an underlying network that was never designed for these demands.

## What Does AI Require from Your Network?


AI places greater demands on nearly every part of your infrastructure. That includes your internet connection, local network, wireless coverage, security, and backup connectivity.


### Reliable Connectivity


Many AI platforms depend on cloud services. Every request made by an employee or customer travels across your internet connection before returning with an answer.


If bandwidth is limited or connections become congested, AI responses become slower. Those delays may only last a few seconds, but they quickly affect productivity and customer experience.


### Low Latency


Latency measures how long it takes information to travel across a network.


AI applications work best when latency stays low.[Voice AI](https://sangoma.com/blog/why-voice-is-becoming-important-again-in-the-era-of-ai-agents/) , virtual receptionists, live transcription, and real-time assistants all depend on quick communication between users and cloud platforms. Higher latency creates noticeable delays that make conversations feel unnatural.


### Enough Capacity for Growing Workloads


AI adds to the existing business applications you’re already using– email, video meetings, file sharing, and[business phone systems](https://sangoma.com/products/communications-platform/) . AI introduces another layer of traffic that shares the same network.


Without enough capacity, every application competes for bandwidth. Performance begins to suffer across the entire business.


## What Does an AI-Ready Network Look Like?


Preparing your business network for AI means making sure every layer of your infrastructure can support today’s workloads while giving your business room to grow tomorrow.


### Modern Switching


As businesses process more data locally, many are upgrading older 1 Gigabit switching infrastructure to 10 Gigabit networks that can better support AI workloads and connected devices. Faster switching improves communication between servers, storage, and users while reducing bottlenecks.


### Intelligent Traffic Management


Technologies such as SD-WAN allow businesses to direct network traffic more intelligently. AI workloads can receive the bandwidth they need without disrupting voice calls, video meetings, or other business-critical applications.


### Strong Wireless Coverage


Phones, tablets, security cameras, smart sensors, AI-enabled devices, and collaboration tools all rely on Wi-Fi. As the number of connected devices increases, businesses need wireless infrastructure that can support higher device density without sacrificing performance.


### Backup Connectivity


A backup internet connection, such as managed 5G failover, helps keep employees connected and AI-powered applications available when the primary connection experiences an outage. Rather than bringing business operations to a halt, traffic automatically shifts to the backup connection until service is restored.


### Integrated Security


AI applications often process customer information, internal documents, and other sensitive business data. That makes[network security](https://sangoma.com/products/managed-security/) an essential part of AI network readiness, not a separate project.


A modern network should include layered security, continuous monitoring, regular updates, and protections that help reduce vulnerabilities while supporting compliance requirements across the business.


## How Can You Tell if Your Business Network Is Ready for AI?


Start by asking these questions:


- Does your internet connection slow down during busy times of the day?


- Do employees regularly experience Wi-Fi issues or poor call quality?


- Can your business continue operating if your primary internet connection goes offline?


- Is network traffic prioritized, or does every application compete equally for bandwidth?


- Has your networking equipment been updated within the past several years?


- Are networking, security, wireless, and connectivity managed separately by multiple vendors?


If several of these questions raise concerns, it may be time to evaluate your infrastructure before expanding your use of AI.


## Why AI Infrastructure Is Becoming a Business Priority


Businesses often think of AI as another software purchase. In reality, AI is becoming part of the infrastructure that supports everyday operations.


Customer service teams rely on AI to answer questions faster. Sales teams use AI to summarize meetings and prepare follow-up emails. Finance teams analyze trends. Healthcare providers document patient interactions. Hotels automate guest requests. Manufacturers monitor equipment using connected devices and AI analytics.


The organizations seeing the greatest value from AI are investing in the infrastructure that allows those tools to perform consistently every day.


## Preparing Your Business Network for AI Doesn’t Have to Be Complicated


The good news is that preparing for AI doesn’t require a complete network replacement.


The first step is understanding how your current infrastructure performs today and whether it can support the AI initiatives you plan to introduce over the next several years. A network assessment often identifies opportunities to improve performance, increase reliability, strengthen security, and reduce future bottlenecks without replacing every component.

## Build the Right Foundation Before You Build on AI


AI has great potential to improve customer service, increase productivity, and help employees work more efficiently. None of those benefits happen consistently without a reliable foundation.
